title: PRD: Graded Mitigation Matrix and Cohorted Evaluation Lifecycle for Optimize
creator: Adele Romero
description: This PRD defines a graded mitigation matrix and a cohorted evaluation lifecycle for Optimize evaluations. The goal is to provide deterministic, actionable acceptance checks for model changes (new weights, quantization, kernel updates, or prompt tuning) so product teams can ship upgrades with bounded risk. This document covers promptset design, sampling requirements, composite signal construction, A/B decision gating, concrete regression thresholds, and an ordered mitigation (de-escalation) flow that runs automatically during canary and staged rollouts.
background: Optimize runs continuous evals against production-like prompt cohorts. Current alerts are noisy and leave engineers to make ad-hoc rollback decisions. We need a reproducible decision framework that ties signal degradations to concrete actions (traffic hold, reduced exposure, quality remediation) and that supports staged rollouts across customer cohorts and deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private).
goals: Define a small set of composite signals that capture both utility and safety regressions
Specify promptset cohorts (core, long-tail, safety-sensitive) and minimum sample sizes for statistical validity
Prescribe A/B gating rules with asymmetric tolerance for different signal classes
Provide an ordered mitigation matrix (from soft fallbacks to full rollback) and the automated triggers that map signals -> actions
Document operational runbook for on-call and PM review during a failing canary
success_metrics: Reduce manual rollbacks by 40% in first quarter after rollout
Catch 95% of severe safety regressions during canary phase with <2 false positives per month
Average time from anomaly alert to mitigation action decreased to <15 minutes for P1 regressions
Maintained overall latency SLO (p95) during canary episodes
evaluation_design: We will run a two-stage evaluation: an isolated offline run over the labeled prompt cohorts (daily) and an online shadow canary against a small percent of traffic for staged validation. Offline runs compute composite signals; online runs validate those signals with real user distributions and trigger the mitigation matrix when thresholds are exceeded.
promptset_strategy: Core prompts: 2k deterministic prompts representing the most frequent API routes and top customers
Long-tail prompts: 5k sampled prompts covering low-frequency but high-variance inputs (regex-based and language diversity)
Safety-sensitive prompts: 1k curated prompts flagged by Trust & Safety and legal teams
Regression harness: 500 adversarial prompts synthesized from prior failure modes and model hallucinations
sampling_requirements: Offline runs: full promptset each night; require >95% completion without timeouts
Online canary: start at 0.5% traffic for 4 hours, then 2% for 12 hours, then 10% for 24 hours if no blocking signals
Minimum per-cohort sample size for statistical tests: 200 responses at the first canary step, 1000 at the 10% step
Confidence: use two-sided tests at alpha=0.01 for core signals, alpha=0.05 for long-tail
signal_list: Utility-ROUGE-like: token-level ngram and paraphrase overlap vs. golden responses (where available)
Semantic drift: embedding cosine shift per-prompt cohort compared to baseline distribution
Calibration/regression: change in answer format compliance (JSON schema failures, tool-calling mismatches)
Hallucination proxy: named-entity hallucination rate using reference knowledge checks
Latency degradation: p95 and p99 increases relative to baseline
Error surface: streaming disconnects, truncated outputs, decode-time exceptions
Safety triggers: explicit policy-violating classifications from automated safety classifiers
Cost delta: per-token cost increase due to longer generations or runtime inefficiency
thresholds: Blocking (auto-rollback): safety triggers increase >1.0% absolute on safety-sensitive cohort AND rate of new critical classifier hits doubled vs baseline
Severe (auto-hold traffic): composite safety + hallucination proxy worsens by >30% relative change on core cohort
Degraded (manual review required): utility metric drops >10% on core cohort OR p95 latency increases >2x
Acceptable drift (informational): semantic drift >2 standard deviations on long-tail but no utility or safety degradation
ab_criteria: Primary gate: require non-inferiority on utility metrics (delta <= 3%) on core cohort at 95% confidence to pass A/B
Secondary gate: safety regression must be statistically indistinguishable (p>0.01) on safety-sensitive cohort
Tolerance asymmetry: safety regressions carry >3x weight compared to marginal utility improvements when computing composite score
Sequential testing: stop-on-fail rule during A/B—if any blocking threshold hit at interim analysis, halt rollout
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback: auto-rollback when Blocking threshold met during online canary
Escalated rollback: if Severe threshold persists beyond trailing 3-hour window despite mitigation steps, perform full rollback
User-facing incidents: any verified customer complaint tied to quality degradation escalates to manual rollback decision within 30 minutes
Cumulative degradation: if two separate cohorts exceed Degraded thresholds within 24 hours, trigger a rollback review and default to rollback unless PM approves mitigation
monitoring_playbook: On-call receives automated alert with signal deltas, cohort breakdowns, and link to the canary run dashboard. First responder runs quick triage: confirm signal validity, check for infra incidents, verify sample sizes. If blocking/severe conditions detected, follow graded mitigation matrix: 1) reduce canary weight to previous safe step; 2) enable model-level fallback to prior version for affected routes; 3) apply promptset-specific prefix adjustments (short-term); 4) rollback. PM and Engineering must be paged on Severe/Blocking. Document action and timeline in the incident channel and append to the canary run artifact.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Offline validation — nightly eval for 7 days against baseline to build stable baselines
Stage 1: Canary 0.5% traffic — monitor for 4 hours (auto-abort on Blocking)
Stage 2: Canary 2% traffic — 12 hours, enable extended signal collection and human spot-check
Stage 3: Canary 10% traffic — 24 hours, execute A/B statistical analysis
Stage 4: Progressive ramp to 100% with staggered region and tenant controls if all gates pass
notes: We intentionally pick conservative alpha for core signals to lower false negatives on critical regressions.
Security review needed for safety-sensitive cohort because it contains proprietary compliance prompts for regulated customers.
Implementation will require two infra pieces: (1) per-cohort streaming metrics pipeline, (2) safe auto-rollback API with audit logging. Coordinate with ENG infra owners.
This PRD focuses on quantitative gates; manual spot-check workflows for ambiguous failures will be curated in the playbook.
